thread:
Aisha (Product): heads-up — AtlasHealth just sent an inbound ask: 7-year audit-log retention + BYOK for audit logs (customer-managed keys, FIPS-level HSM preferred). They want this in contract negotiations next quarter. Can we triage feasibility and minimal launch criteria?

Ravi (Security): ack. long retention + BYOK for logs has regulatory weight. questions: do they need tenant-level key separation or just envelope keys? also need chain-of-custody for exported evidence.

Keiko (CS): AtlasHealth insists on tenant-isolated keys (one per customer) and a handoff flow for key escrow to auditors. They're a fin/health hybrid; legal will require proof-of-export capabilities.

Marta (Eng Infra): technically we can support per-tenant CMEK for the audit pipeline, but ops + cost concerns: storing 7y of logs in hot tier is expensive. need to define retention buckets (hot, warm, cold) + search SLA for each.

Daniel (SRE): +1 on buckets. For MVP we can keep 90d hot (search <500ms), 2y warm (search via async job <30s), 7y cold (export-only, retrieval within 24h). That keeps cost predictable.

Owen (Finance): note: AtlasHealth quoted 7y will increase storage by ~4x vs current assumptions. we should surface unit costs and a contract uplift. also BYOK HSM integrations add one-time integration effort.

Aisha (Product): propose we scope an MVP that covers the MUST-haves for sales/legal to sign: 1) BYOK for audit logs (tenant keys), 2) exportable evidence bundle (signed manifest) for upto 7y, 3) retention buckets + clear SLAs, 4) KMS integration guide + runbook. anything else mandatory?

Ravi (Security): add: crypto attestation docs + threat model for key handling. must include key rotation policy, and explicit statement that Redwood never holds plaintext after envelope.

Marta (Eng Infra): implementation notes: 
- BYOK handshake: initial key wrap + periodic attest (30d).
- Storage encryption: data encrypted at rest with tenant CMEK; metadata signed.
- Export API: /v1/audit-exports with parameters {tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, destination_s3} and signed manifest.

Example config snippet for engineers: 
```
keystore: {
  tenant_id: "atlas-123",
  kms_provider: "aws-kms",
  key_id: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd-...",
  escrow: true
}
retention: {
  hot_days: 90,
  warm_days: 730,
  cold_days: 2555
}
```

Keiko (CS): can we add a capability matrix for sales: checkbox columns for BYOK, export API, retrieval SLA, SOC2 evidence? Sales needs a one-pager.

Daniel (SRE): operational constraints: cold retrieval will be a job that pulls from glacier-like storage -> IAM paths + additional auth for export. We need a throttling policy to prevent huge cross-tenant exports.

Aisha (Product): prioritization thoughts: MVP scope = BYOK handshake + exportable evidence + retention buckets with clear SLAs. Post-MVP: long-term UI for customer retention settings, KMS multi-cloud (GCP/azure) parity, FIPS/HSM vendor attestation. Does that align?

Ravi (Security): yes. also mark FIPS/HSM as enterprise-only feature gated behind contract + security review.

Owen (Finance): require pricing model for 7y retention (per-GB tiered + retrieval fees). I'll draft a proposed uplift and share by EOD Fri.

Marta (Eng Infra): rough engineering estimate for MVP: 6 weeks (BYOK handshake + backend + export API) + 2 weeks SRE runbook and tests. If we include multi-KMS parity add 3 more weeks.

Keiko (CS): legal will need sample contract language. I'll coordinate with legal and feed back exact wording.

Aisha (Product): action items: 
- Ravi: security attestation checklist + threat model (owner: Ravi) — due 2025-02-09
- Marta: tech design doc + example API + initial estimate (owner: Marta) — due 2025-02-05
- Daniel: runbook and retention SLA ops playbook draft (owner: Daniel) — due 2025-02-12
- Owen: pricing uplift + cost model (owner: Owen) — due 2025-01-31
- Keiko: customer contract language and AtlasHealth liaison (owner: Keiko) — due 2025-02-03

Ravi (Security): acked. I'll include explicit statements about never-storing plaintext and rotation.

Marta (Eng Infra): I'll open an RFC today: /rfc/byok-audit-retention. Tagging @deploy-bot to schedule a staging rollout window once implemented.

deploy-bot: deployment window request queued. Please add env:staging test plan and required canary thresholds.

Aisha (Product): thanks all — I'll add this to roadmap candidate pool and flag as "sales‑triggered enterprise". If we get verbal commitment from AtlasHealth this week we'll move to prioritized sprint in Feb.

Keiko (CS): pinging AtlasHealth now, will confirm whether tenant-level keys are non-negotiable.

Daniel (SRE): quick question: do we need retention search for cold beyond export? if legal wants partial search it complicates indexing. I recommend export-only for cold.

Ravi (Security): agree with export-only for cold. add that exported bundles must be signed with tenant key and include hash manifest.

Aisha (Product): final note: for launch criteria (MVP) we'll require: 
- successful BYOK handshake test with one pilot tenant, 
- export API test with manifest validation, 
- cost uplift signoff from finance, 
- signed security attestation doc.

Owen (Finance): noted. will include retrieval pricing and an example invoice line item in my uplift.

Marta (Eng Infra): created /rfc/byok-audit-retention (link: https://go.redwood/rfc/byok-audit-retention). comments welcome.

Keiko (CS): AtlasHealth replied: tenant-level keys required, pilot timeline wants June. they asked for a compliance one-pager by next Tues.

Aisha (Product): ok — move timeline forward. We'll reconvene Mon to confirm tradeoffs vs sprint capacity. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
